data.body:
Phase 1 RCA and OSS consensus (before edits).

Observed mechanism: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` expands four cells (Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13, macOS 3.13). Every cell executes the same default and integration pytest selections; line 751 applies `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered` to every non-macOS cell. `pyproject.toml` supplies `branch = true` and `fail_under = 70`, so Ubuntu independently traces and enforces the same floor three times. A production-source search found no `sys.version` or `sys.version_info` branch; interpreter compatibility remains covered by retaining all three cells.

Dynamic discriminating experiment on merged ead96799ce, same macOS host/check-out, `tests/unit`, 3 workers, identical options and 10,293 passed / 42 skipped every run. Warm-up A=542.51s (excluded). Declared A-B-B-A-A-B samples: A coverage real/user/sys = 532.59/564.74/657.13s, 511.16/550.16/619.71s, 508.48/549.98/613.24s. B no-coverage = 483.50/488.19/593.52s, 477.16/485.91/580.84s, 473.14/482.66/580.12s. median(A)=511.16s; median(B)=477.16s; local_delta=34.00 wall seconds per uninstrumented compatibility cell. Median user CPU delta is 64.25s and median system CPU delta 38.87s. This confirms coverage tracing—not different tests—is a real runner-occupancy cost. It does not claim critical-path savings because macOS already omits coverage.

Defect legitimacy: the explicit session contract requires lowering runner occupancy without losing tests/assertions/OS/Python/behavioral coverage. Duplicate measurement is not coverage breadth. Expected post-fix behavior: all four cells retain both pytest tiers; only Ubuntu 3.13 traces branch coverage and enforces the unchanged floor; 3.11/3.12/macOS execute the same tests uninstrumented.

Ticket precedent/rejection check: closed `ropeable-hydrated-siskin` already accepted removing duplicate macOS tracing while retaining its tests. `coercive-paediatric-bug` rejects parallelism that does not reduce aggregate runner use; this change reduces aggregate traced work. No tracker record rejects primary-cell coverage collection.

OSS research, current 2026-08-14: Django `.github/workflows/coverage_tests.yml` uses one dedicated Ubuntu/Python 3.14 coverage job (https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/.github/workflows/coverage_tests.yml); NumPy `.github/workflows/linux.yml` lines 106-140 uses one Ubuntu/Python 3.12 full-suite coverage job while broader compatibility jobs are uninstrumented (https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/main/.github/workflows/linux.yml); SciPy `.github/workflows/linux.yml` lines 307-368 confines coverage to one prerelease/dependency configuration while its broader Linux matrix is uninstrumented (https://github.com/scipy/scipy/blob/main/.github/workflows/linux.yml). All are active, unarchived, popular projects. No workflow comment or issue-linked rationale rejecting selective coverage was found. Consensus threshold passes 3/3, so the operator-approved remediation is unlocked.

Caller/dependency sweep: the coverage expression is consumed only by the default-suite command; branch/fail-under remain centralized in pyproject.toml. No behavioral caller depends on three identical reports. Back-out remains a Gerrit revert restoring the all-Ubuntu condition and documentation.
